messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The failing test `testNullRecordSeparatorCsv106` creates a CSVFormat with `newFormat(';')`, sets `withSkipHeaderRecord(true)`, and `withHeader("H1", "H2")`. The test calls `format("A", "B")` and expects the result not to end with "null".

Examining the code:

- `CSVFormat.newFormat(';')` returns a CSVFormat instance with the recordSeparator field set to `null` (line 262).
- The CSVFormat constructor (`CSVFormat(...)`) takes `recordSeparator` as one of the parameters and assigns it directly to the instance field without defaulting it (line 307-308).
- Using `withHeader(...)` constructs a new CSVFormat instance preserving existing fields but replaces the header and reuses the original `recordSeparator` (line 752-755). Since the original recordSeparator is `null`, it remains null.
- `CSVFormat.format(Object...)` creates a StringWriter and a CSVPrinter with this CSVFormat, then prints the record.
- The `CSVPrinter.println()` method is called after printing the record. It calls `format.getRecordSeparator()` to append the record separator to the output (lines 323-327).
- `getRecordSeparator()` returns the `recordSeparator` field directly (line 487-488).
- Since the recordSeparator is `null` (never set), `out.append(recordSeparator)` translates to appending `"null"` (the string representation of null in Java) to the output.
- Hence, the final formatted string ends with `"null"`, causing the test to fail the assertion `assertFalse(formatStr.endsWith("null"))`.

The root cause is that the default record separator is `null` and nobody sets a non-null default separator. The `println()` naïvely appends this null value as a string "null" when printing the record separator.

This matches the bug report description that formatting adds an unwanted "null" at the end.

No relevant info is found from the recent unrelated bug report.

This diagnosis concludes the bug happens because the `recordSeparator` is null by default in the CSVFormat created by `newFormat(';')`, and this causes the CSVPrinter to append the string "null" as record separator instead of nothing or a correct separator such as a newline. The fix would involve ensuring a suitable non-null record separator is used or `println()` method checks for null before appending the record separator.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
